input.question: Under SEBI ICDR Regulations 2018, if a warrant is allotted on 1 January 2024, what is the latest calendar date on which the warrant holder can exercise the option to acquire equity shares, assuming the warrant exercise price is paid on the last permissible day?

statements.text: Under SEBI ICDR Regulations 2018, the tenure of warrants issued in an initial public offer shall not exceed eighteen months from the date of their allotment.
The warrant holder shall exercise the option to acquire equity shares against each warrant within three months from the date of payment of warrant exercise price.

If a warrant is allotted on 1 January 2024, and the warrant exercise price is paid on the last permissible day (which can be up to eighteen months from allotment), then the latest calendar date on which the warrant holder can exercise the option to acquire shares is three months from that payment date, i.e., eighteen months plus three months from 1 January 2024, totaling twenty-one months from the allotment date, which is 1 October 2025.

An application filed after the initial sixty-day period but within the next one hundred and twenty calendar days (the delayed period) can be considered with an increased settlement amount, but no application will be accepted after one hundred and twenty calendar days beyond the initial sixty-day window.

Therefore, the total maximum number of calendar days from the date of service of a show cause notice within which a settlement application can be filed, including the initial sixty-day period and the delayed period, is 180 days.

No such delayed application shall be considered if the application is filed after one hundred and twenty calendar days from the expiry of the sixty-day period.

statements.text: Under SEBI (Issue and Listing of Municipal Debt Securities) Regulations 2015, when rolling over municipal debt securities, the issuer must give a twenty one days' notice of the proposed roll-over to the holders.
If the roll-over notice is dispatched on 5 May 2025, the earliest date on which the roll-over can take effect, assuming all holders consent within the notice period, is 26 May 2025.

evidence.text: Where the issuer desires to roll-over the municipal debt securities issued, it shall do so only upon passing of a special resolution to that effect and give twenty one days' notice of the proposed roll over to the holders of municipal debt securities: Provided that, if the holders of municipal debt securities do not provide consent for the proposed roll over within the notice period, the issuer shall redeem the municipal debt securities of such holders.

input.question: Under SEBI (InvIT) Regulations 2014, if an entity associated with the InvIT has a gross turnover of ten crore rupees, what is the maximum permissible pecuniary relationship an independent director candidate may have with it â€” applying the two per cent cap or the fifty lakh rupee cap?

statements.text: Under SEBI (InvIT) Regulations 2014, the material pecuniary relationship of an independent director candidate with an entity associated with the InvIT is capped at the lower of two percent of the entity's gross turnover or fifty lakh rupees.
If the entity associated with the InvIT has a gross turnover of ten crore rupees, two percent of this turnover is twenty lakh rupees, which is less than fifty lakh rupees.

Therefore, for an entity with a gross turnover of ten crore rupees, the maximum permissible pecuniary relationship an independent director candidate may have is capped at twenty lakh rupees, applying the two per cent cap rather than the fifty lakh rupee cap.

input.question: Does the original definition of 'large value fund for accredited investors' and the November 2025-amended definition impose the same minimum investment threshold per investor?

statements.text: The original definition (before November 2025 amendment) of 'large value fund for accredited investors' imposed a minimum investment threshold of seventy crore rupees per investor.
The definition as amended effective November 19, 2025, lowered the minimum investment threshold per investor to twenty-five crore rupees.
Therefore, the original and November 2025-amended definitions do not impose the same minimum investment threshold per investor; the amended threshold is lower.

evidence.text:
Passage A:
Regulation 2(1)(pa) (before November 2025 amendment): 'large value fund for accredited investors' means an Alternative Investment Fund or scheme of an Alternative Investment Fund in which each investor (other than the Manager, Sponsor, employees or directors of the Alternative Investment Fund or employees or directors of the Manager) is an accredited investor and invests not less than seventy crore rupees.

Passage B:
Regulation 2(1)(pa) (as amended w.e.f. 19-11-2025): 'large value fund for accredited investors' means an Alternative Investment Fund or scheme of an Alternative Investment Fund in which each investor (other than the Manager, Sponsor, employees or directors of the Alternative Investment Fund or employees or directors of the Manager) is an accredited investor and invests not less than twenty-five crore rupees.

input.question: An acquirer holds 28% voting rights in a listed company with 10 crore total shares outstanding. What is the maximum number of additional shares they can acquire in financial year 2024-25 without triggering a mandatory open offer under Regulation 3(2)?

statements.text: As per Regulation 3(2), an acquirer holding 25% or more but less than the maximum permissible non-public shareholding can acquire additional shares within any financial year only up to 5% of the voting rights without triggering an open offer.
The acquirer currently holds 28% voting rights, which is above 25%, so the maximum additional voting rights they can acquire without triggering an open offer in financial year 2024-25 is 5%.
With a total of 10 crore shares outstanding, 5% corresponds to 0.5 crore shares.
